verses.49:5: {congregate} os seus santos: * {ordinant} a sua aliança sobre os sacrifícios.
verses.49:6: E os céus anunciarão a sua justiça: * porque Deus é juiz.
verses.49:7: Ouve, meu povo, e eu falarei; Israel, e {testificabor}: * Deus, o teu Deus, sou eu.
verses.49:8: Não te repreenderei pelos teus sacrifícios: * {autem} estão sempre {conspectu_meo}.
verses.49:10: Porque são minhas todas as feras {silvarum}: * {jumenta} nos montes, e os bois.
verses.49:11: {cognovi} todas as aves do céu: * e a beleza do campo está comigo.
verses.49:12: Se eu tiver fome, não te direi: * pois meu é {orbis}, e a sua plenitude.
verses.49:13: Acaso comerei {carnes} dos touros? * ou beberei o sangue {hircorum}?
verses.49:14: {immola} a Deus um sacrifício de louvor: * e paga ao Altíssimo os teus votos.
verses.49:15: E invoca-me no dia da tribulação: * eu te libertarei, e tu me {honorificabis}.
verses.49:16: Ao pecador, porém, disse Deus: * Por que tu {enarras} {justitias}, e tomas a minha aliança {peros}?
verses.49:17: Tu, porém, {odisti} a disciplina: * e lançaste para trás as minhas palavras:
verses.49:18: Se vias um ladrão, corrias com ele: * e com os adúlteros {portionem}.
verses.49:19: A tua boca abundou em malícia: * e a tua língua {concinnabat} enganos.

decisions.why: The stylist heard the opening *O Deus dos deuses* as the vocative *Ó*, re-parsed at *falou*. Putting the verb first (natural Portuguese order, D2) removes the misreading and keeps the Latin order of the names, *Deus deórum* before *Dóminus*. His own line (*Falou o Senhor, o Deus dos deuses*) swaps the two names; not needed.

options.label: Falou o Deus dos deuses, o Senhor

forms.order1: Falou o Deus dos deuses, o Senhor

options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist's verb-first order, the Latin's order of the names.

options.label: O Deus dos deuses, o Senhor, falou

forms.order1: O Deus dos deuses, o Senhor, falou

options.note: draft 1, the Latin order; heard as a vocative first.

options.label: Falou o Senhor, o Deus dos deuses

forms.order1: Falou o Senhor, o Deus dos deuses

options.note: the stylist's line; the names reversed.

decisions.latin: et vocávit terram … Advocábit cælum desúrsum
decisions.why: Two Latin verbs, and two Greek ones (ἐκάλεσεν / προσκαλέσεται): the simple verb and its compound. The simple *vocáre* is *chamar* (the vocáre row, 48:12); the compound *advocáre* takes *convocar*, which says the summons to a court the psalm is staging. MS1932 has *convocou* for the first and *Chamará* for the second, the other way round; DRB *called … shall call*. Keeping simple → simple and compound → compound follows the Latin's own shape.

options.label: chamou … Convocará
options.note: Ruling: simple and compound kept apart, as the Latin and the Greek have them.

options.label: convocou … Chamará
options.note: MS1932's pair; it gives the compound's sense to the simple verb.

options.label: chamou … Chamará
options.note: DRB's one verb; loses the compound.

decisions.latin: A solis ortu usque ad occásum
decisions.why: A formula: 112:3 has the same words (*A solis ortu usque ad occásum, laudábile nomen Dómini*) and 106:3 a near form (*A solis ortu, et occásu*) — grep. *nascer do sol* is the plain noun for *ortus solis*. For *occásus*, *poente* is the plain word; *ocaso* is the cognate and is understood, but literary. *Desde … até* is the Portuguese of *a … usque ad*. No article-less *sol posto*.

options.label: Desde o nascer do sol até o poente

forms.ortu: Desde o nascer do sol até o poente

options.label: Desde o nascer do sol até o ocaso

forms.ortu: Desde o nascer do sol até o ocaso

options.label: Do oriente até o ocidente
options.note: MS1932 *desde o oriente até ao ocidente*: the points of the compass for the sun's course — the image of the sun is lost.

decisions.why: The spécies row left 49:1 to this psalm. spécies → *beleza* (46:5) and decor → *esplendor* (20:6, 25:8, 29:8, 44:12) are both kept, so two nouns stand as the Latin's two do (the Greek ἡ εὐπρέπεια τῆς ὡραιότητος is also two). The line has no verb in the Latin, and none is supplied (MS1932 supplies *virá*; DRB none): the colon is a cry, and the next verse gives the verb (*Deus maniféste véniet*).

options.label: o esplendor da sua beleza
options.note: MS1932's order of ideas (*o resplendor da sua formosura*); the two rows' words would then stand for the wrong Latin nouns.

options.label: virá a beleza do seu esplendor

forms.species: virá a beleza do seu esplendor

options.note: MS1932 supplies a verb; the Latin has none.

decisions.why: ἐμφανῶς, openly, in plain sight. *manifestamente* is the cognate (MS1932) and keeps the syllable count of the Latin colon exactly (8/8); it is long but plain, and stressed on the penultimate before the asterisk. *às claras* is lighter and more spoken; *visivelmente* explains a little. v2: the blind reader listed *manifestamente* as unknown, and the stylist found it legal; *abertamente* is the plain word for ἐμφανῶς and keeps the sense (openly, not in secret).

options.label: abertamente
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist; ἐμφανῶς, openly. *manifestamente* was unknown to the blind reader and heavy to the stylist.

options.label: às claras
options.note: lighter; puts the colon at 6 syllables.

options.label: manifestamente
options.note: draft 1; MS1932; unknown to the blind reader.

options.label: visivelmente
options.note: the Greek's sense; one step from the Latin word.

decisions.why: The silére / tacére row keeps two Latin verbs apart: silére → *ficar em silêncio*, tacére → *calar-se* (49:20 *e eu me calei*). Here the Greek differs too (παρασιωπήσεται / ἐσίγησα). The stylist asks *não se calará* (shorter, oxytone close); refused, because it would make 49:3 and 49:20 one verb where the Latin has two.

exardéscere → *inflamar-se* (the row; 38:4 *um fogo se inflamará*); *arder* is concaléscere's in 38:4, where the two stand in one verse. The stylist asks *arderá* (plainer); refused for that collision, kept as the option.

decisions.latin: Ignis in conspéctu ejus exardéscet … in conspéctu meo sunt semper
decisions.why: *in conspéctu* is still open (D22). The finished psalms say *na sua presença* where the one in whose sight it is, is God (17:7b, 17:13, 21:28b, 21:30, 40:13, 118:168–170), and *à vista de* mostly for men (9:26a, 15:8, 37:18). Here both are God: the fire before him, and God speaking of the holocausts *always before me*. *na sua presença / na minha presença* follows the finished psalms; *à vista dele* (the row's proposal) is the option.

options.label: na sua presença … na minha presença
à vista dele … à minha vista
diante dele … diante de mim
options.note: MS1932 (*diante de mim*), DRB *before him / in my sight*; loses the noun.

decisions.latin: holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper
decisions.why: The blind reader heard *porém* as a contrast that turns the line into a reproach (I do not rebuke you, *but* your holocausts…). The Latin *autem* is here a weak connective: the holocausts are not blamed, they are always before God (DRB *and*). *e* says that.
válidus is strong, powerful (καταιγὶς σφόδρα, a very great storm). *violenta* (MS1932) says the force of a storm as Portuguese says it; *forte* is the plainest word but is the *fortis* row's (7:12).

D42 settled discérnere → *separar* (42:1 *separai a minha causa*). The Greek is διακρῖναι, to judge by telling apart — which is what *separar* says of a judge who divides one from another (cf. the separating of sheep and goats). DRB and MS1932 say *to judge*; *julgar* is judicáre's (7:9b, 42:1 — in 42:1 both verbs stand side by side, so they must differ). The settled word is kept; *julgar* is the option.

A plural imperative (to the heavens or the ministers of the court — the Latin does not say): *vós*. *Reuni* (the congregári row's verb) is also 'I gathered' — the bare form rule 3 bans, and this colon opens the verse. *Congregai* (the active verb of 15:4b) is safe (past *congreguei*). *illi* → *para ele* (DRB *to him*; MS1932 *diante dele*). v2: the stylist asked *Reuni para ele*; refused, as above (rule 3). *Congregai-lhe* is the option if *para ele* sits awkwardly.

options.label: Congregai-lhe
options.note: shorter; the clitic *lhe* next to *os seus santos* is momentarily ambiguous.

options.label: Reuni para ele
options.note: the congregári row's verb; bare *Reuni* = 'I gathered' (rule 3).

decisions.latin: qui órdinant testaméntum ejus super sacrifícia
decisions.why: τοὺς διατιθεμένους τὴν διαθήκην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ θυσίαις: those who make (ratify) his covenant upon sacrifices. ordináre is to set in order, establish. *firmar uma aliança* is the Portuguese idiom for making a covenant, and says the setting-in-place of ordináre without explaining; *ordenar* is the cognate but is heard in Brazil as 'command' (as the ordinátio row found, *ordenação* is holy orders). *super sacrifícia* → *sobre os sacrifícios*, the preposition kept (MS1932's *por meio de* explains). *os que* makes the relative a second vocative-like apposition after the colon break, easier to say than a bare *que*. Cost: *firmar* is also statúere's word elsewhere (118:38); here statúere (49:21) is *pôr*, so they do not meet. v2: the Latinist (minor) asked *ordenam* (ordain, set in order); refused because the blind reader heard the covenant rightly with *firmam*, while *ordenar* is heard first as command. It stays option 2.

options.label: os que fizeram
options.note: MS1932 *fizeram aliança*; the Latin's present lost.

decisions.why: διαμαρτύρομαί σοι: I will bear solemn witness to you (DRB *I will testify to thee*). *eu te darei testemunho* keeps the dative and the noun of witness (MS1932 the same). *testemunharei contra ti* is the Hebrew's sense (*bāk*, against you) and not the Latin's *tibi*. The *audi* of the first half governs *Israël* too; it is not repeated (MS1932 adds a second *ouve*).

options.label: eu testemunharei contra ti
options.note: the Hebrew's 'against'; not the Latin's dative.

decisions.latin: neque de grégibus tuis hircos … aut sánguinem hircórum potábo
decisions.why: hircus is the he-goat (χίμαρος / τράγος; DRB *he goats … goats*). *bode* is the plain Brazilian word for the male goat; MS1932's *cabritos* are kids. One word in both verses, as the Latin has one.

enarráre → *narrar* (the row; 18:2 *Os céus narram*). The stylist asks *proclamas* (stronger than a storyteller's *narrar*); refused: *proclamar* is prædicáre's (the enarráre row). The blind reader listed *narras* as unknown, which is surprising for a common verb; the form stands.

decisions.latin: Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos
decisions.why: The stylist: the Latin order puts the object last, like an afterthought. Natural order is grammar (D2); taken. His *aceitarei* for *receberei* is refused: accípere → *receber* (the row).

options.label: Não receberei bezerros da tua casa

forms.order9: Não receberei bezerros da tua casa

options.label: Não receberei da tua casa bezerros

forms.order9: Não receberei da tua casa bezerros

options.label: Não aceitarei bezerros da tua casa

forms.order9: Não aceitarei bezerros da tua casa

options.note: the stylist's verb; not accípere's row.

decisions.why: silva, the wood (δρυμός, thicket). *selvas* is the cognate and MS1932's word; in Brazil it calls up the Amazon, but that is still wild forest, which is what the line needs. *matas* is the everyday Brazilian word; *bosques* is too tame for *feræ*. feræ → *feras* (the oves/boves row keeps *feras* for béstiæ / feræ); juménta → *os animais* (the juménta row: *jumento* is a donkey in Brazil).

juménta → *os animais* (the row; κτήνη, as 8:8 pécora). The Latinist (minor) asks *o gado*: the row names it as its option, but here *o gado … e os bois* would say cattle twice, since oxen are cattle. Refused, kept as the option.
D30 settled *orbis terræ* → *o mundo* (*orbe* unknown to two blind readers). The Latinist (minor) asks *o orbe da terra*; refused under D30.

The Latin plural *carnes* is flesh as food; the carnes row has *as carnes* for a man's own flesh (118:120). The stylist heard *as carnes dos touros* as a butcher's counter; flesh as food is singular in Portuguese. Number is grammar (D2, as D29 did with *sangue*); taken. The singular also matches *o sangue* in the second colon.

options.label: a carne
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist; MS1932 *a carne dos touros*.

decisions.why: A perfect with present sense (ἔγνωκα, 'I have come to know' = I know). DRB *I know*, MS1932 *Conheço*. In Portuguese *Conheci* reads as a past event ('I met'), so the tense yields to the sense (grammar, D2). The verb stays *conhecer* (the cognóscere row).

options.label: Conheci
options.note: the Latin's tense; heard as a past event.

decisions.why: immoláre (θῦσον) is to sacrifice a victim. *Imola* keeps the Latin's word and its weight — the psalm has just refused bulls and goats, and now names a sacrifice of another kind with the sacrificial verb. MS1932 *Oferece* is softer and makes it a general offering. The tu imperative *imola* is plain. v2: the blind reader listed *Imola* as unknown; kept — it is the Latin's word and the psalm's point (a sacrifice of another kind); *Oferece* is one touch away.

decisions.latin: et honorificábis me … Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me
decisions.why: One verb twice (δοξάσεις / δοξάσει), and the psalm turns on it: God asks to be honoured, and the sacrifice of praise honours him. *honrar* (36:20 *honrados*; MS1932 *honrarás … honrará*) keeps it apart from glorificáre → *glorificar* (the row). DRB has *glorify* for both, following the Greek; the Latin has chosen *honorificáre*.

The plural justítiæ row names 49:16 as a place to decide locally. The Greek is τὰ δικαιώματά μου (ordinances), as at 17:23, where the finished psalm kept *as suas justiças*. Kept the same here: the Latin's word, and the echo with 49:6 *a sua justiça*. *os meus preceitos* would say the Greek's sense but would take *preceitos*, which D15 reserves for justificatiónes; *mandamentos* (MS1932) is mandáta's. enarráre → *narrar* (the row; the second of its two places).

decisions.latin: et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum
decisions.why: διὰ στόματός σου, 'through your mouth': to take the covenant upon one's lips. The Portuguese idiom is *tomar na boca* (DRB *in thy mouth*; MS1932 *na tua boca*); *pela tua boca* keeps the preposition but *tomar pela boca* is not said. assúmere → *tomar* here: the assúmere row's *recolher* (17:17, 26:10) is for a person taken up and does not fit a thing taken on the lips; noted for the row. v2: the Latinist (minor) asked *pela tua boca*; refused for the reason above, kept as option 2.

decisions.latin: Tu vero odísti disciplínam: et projecísti sermónes meos retrórsum
decisions.why: odísse is a perfect with present sense, and the 2026-09-21 review made 118:104 *odeio* for that reason. But here it stands beside the perfect *projecísti* in an indictment told in the past (vias, corrias, fizeste), and the Greek is the aorist ἐμίσησας; DRB *thou hast hated … hast cast*. The past keeps the two verbs of the verse in one tense; the present (MS1932 *aborreces*) is the option. 44:8 *odísti iniquitátem* → *odiaste* is the precedent for the past beside another perfect.

decisions.latin: et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas
decisions.why: μετὰ μοιχῶν τὴν μερίδα σου ἐτίθεις: 'you set your portion with adulterers' — cast in your lot with them. pórtio → *porção* (the row); pónere → *pôr*. The literal words are sayable and the sense is heard; MS1932 *fazias sociedade* and DRB *hast been a partaker* explain. v2: the stylist named 49:18 the worst line and asked *punhas a tua parte*; the blind reader heard it only roughly as 'you took part'. Refused for the pórtio row (kept apart from pars → *parte*); *parte* does not make the idiom any more Portuguese — *pôr a parte com* is no more said than *pôr a porção*. Kept as option 2; if Gustavo wants the sense heard plainly, *tomavas a tua parte* is the one to take.

options.label: punhas a tua parte
options.note: stylist (his worst line): *parte* plainer; pars's word (15:5).

decisions.why: concinnáre: to join fitly together, arrange (L&S); the Greek περιέπλεκεν, wove, entwined. *tramar* is the weaver's word (the *trama* is the weft) and is how Portuguese says contriving deceit; MS1932's *urdir* is the warp and the same image, but bookish. Proposed for 57:3 *injustítias … concínnant* too.

decisions.latin: et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum
decisions.why: scándalum → *tropeço* (the row; 48:14, 118:165): *escândalo* is a public outrage in Portuguese. *pôr tropeço contra* keeps pónere and the preposition; MS1932 *armavas laços* changes the image (laço is láqueus).

options.label: punhas um tropeço
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist; the article is grammar.

options.label: punhas tropeço
options.note: draft 1; the bare noun, clipped to the stylist.

decisions.latin: Existimásti, iníque, quod ero tui símilis
decisions.why: *iníque* can be the adverb (unjustly) or the vocative of iníquus (O wicked one). The Vulgate-family witnesses both read the adverb (DRB *Thou thoughtest unjustly*; MS1932 *Pensaste iniquamente*), and 43:18 *iníque non égimus* → *não agimos iniquamente* is the psalter's adverb. The Greek ὑπέλαβες ἀνομίαν has a noun object and settles nothing for the Latin. Ruled for the adverb with the two witnesses; the vocative is the option. *quod ero* → *que eu seria*: Portuguese puts the future in the past after a past verb (grammar). existimáre → *pensar* (MS1932); æstimári → *ser tido* is another build. v2: the stylist found *iniquamente* bookish and asked the vocative; the blind reader listed it unknown and heard 'wrongly'. Refused: the stylist's wording takes the other reading of the Latin, which both Vulgate-family witnesses reject; it stays option 2 and the choice between the two readings is for Gustavo.

decisions.latin: árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam
decisions.why: *státuam* has no object in the Latin (the Greek παραστήσω has none either; the Hebrew 'set in order before your eyes' has an implied one). DRB keeps it bare (*and set before thy face*); MS1932 supplies *(tudo)*, marked as his gloss. Supplying *te* (set you before your own face) or *tudo* (your deeds) would resolve what the Latin leaves open. Kept bare. statúere → *pôr* here: the statúere row's *firmar* is for establishing and does not fit a setting-before. *contra fáciem* → *diante da tua face* (the fácies row). v2: the stylist asked for a neuter *o* (*e o porei*) so the ear is not left waiting; refused, because *o* is heard as 'him' and supplies an object. The Latinist passed the bare form as keeping the Latin's ellipsis.

The oblivísci row takes a direct object (*não esqueci a vossa lei*); with a person Portuguese marks the object with *a*: *esqueceis a Deus*. *vos esqueceis de Deus* (MS1932) is the more common spoken build, and is the option.

decisions.latin: nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat
decisions.why: The *nequándo rápiat* row (7:3): no subject supplied; in 49:22 the one who seizes is God, and the Latin leaves it to be understood; it names no object either (DRB and MS1932 supply *you*). rápere → *arrebatar*; erípere with no source named → *libertar* (the erípere row). *para que não arrebate* keeps both open. v2: the Latinist and the stylist both asked *livre* (the stylist also a subject *ele*). Refused: *livrar* is liberáre's verb, and the erípere row gives *libertar* where no source is named (24:20, 90:15); the Latinist's point, that *liberte* loses the snatch that answers *rápiat*, is fair — the row's other verb, *arranque*, keeps it, and is option 3. The subject is left unnamed by the row (the blind reader still heard God).

options.label: arrebate … liberte
options.note: Ruling; the rápere and erípere rows.

options.label: arrebate … arranque
options.note: the erípere row's other verb; keeps the snatching image the Latinist wants.

decisions.latin: et illic iter, quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei
decisions.why: The Latin has no verb in *illic iter*; Portuguese supplies *está* (grammar, D2). iter → *caminho* (the row). *quo* → *por onde*, lighter than *pelo qual* (MS1932) and the same sense. *illi* → *lhe*, the one who offers the sacrifice of praise. salutáre → *salvação* (D6).

choices.49:1: *Deus deórum, Dóminus*: the two names in apposition, set off with commas (DRB *The God of gods, the Lord*). *locútus est* → *falou*.
choices.49:3: silére → *ficar em silêncio* and tacére (49:20) → *calar-se*: the silére / tacére row keeps two Latin verbs apart; here the Greek differs too (παρασιωπήσεται / ἐσίγησα).
choices.49:3b: exardéscere → *inflamar-se*, *um fogo se inflamará* as 38:4. in circúitu → *ao seu redor* (17:12).
choices.49:6: annuntiáre → *anunciar* (D41). *judex est* → *é juiz*, no article, as the Latin.
choices.49:7: God speaks to Israel, one people: *tu* (rule 3; D17). *Deus, Deus tuus* → *Deus, o teu Deus*, as 44:8.
choices.49:8: árguere → *repreender* (D21), the same verb again in 49:21 as the Latin repeats *árguam te*. *in sacrifíciis* (ἐπί, 'concerning') → *pelos*. holocáustum → *holocausto* (the row).
choices.49:9: accípere → *receber* (the row). vítulus → *bezerro* (the row). Latin order kept (*da tua casa bezerros*), so that the mediant falls on *bezerros*.
choices.49:10: juménta → *os animais* (the row; *jumento* is a donkey).
choices.49:11: volatília cæli → *as aves do céu*; pulchritúdo → *beleza* (D43).
choices.49:12: orbis terræ → *o mundo* (D30); *et plenitúdo ejus* → *e a sua plenitude*, the formula of 23:1. *Si esuríero* → *Se eu tiver fome*.
choices.49:14: vota réddere → *pagar os votos* (21:26). Altíssimus → *Altíssimo* (the row).
choices.49:15: invocáre → *invocar*; éruere with no source → *libertar* (as 24:20 *libertai-me*); *dia da tribulação* as 19:2.
choices.49:16: God now speaks to the sinner, one man: *tu*. *Quare tu* → *Por que tu*, the pronoun kept for its emphasis.
choices.49:17: sermónes → *palavras* (D15). projícere → *lançar*; retrórsum → *para trás* (the retrórsum row).
choices.49:20: *Sedens* → *Sentado*, set off by a comma. *hæc* → *isto*, and the same in 49:22. *fílium matris tuæ* → *o filho da tua mãe*, the Hebraism kept.
choices.49:22: A plural audience (*obliviscímini*): *vós* (rule 3). intellégere → *entender*; *Entendei* is safe (past *entendi*).
choices.49:23: *Sacrifícium laudis* → *O sacrifício de louvor* here (a subject), *um sacrifício de louvor* in 49:14 (an object after an imperative), as 4:6 *um sacrifício de justiça*.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (no Diurnal: not a day-hours psalm). God speaks in the first person from 49:7: to Israel (tu) and then to the sinner (tu); the heavens / the court (49:5) and the forgetful (49:22) are plural (vós). Hard readings: 49:5 *órdinant testaméntum super sacrifícia*; 49:21 *iníque* (adverb or vocative) and the object-less *státuam*; 49:17 the tense of *odísti*; 49:1b the verbless *spécies decóris*.

Hard checks pass. Soft length flags accepted: 49:3 second colon +4 (*ficar em silêncio* is the silére row's, kept apart from tacére → *calar-se* in 49:20); 49:7 −3, 49:20 −3, 49:22 −3 (Portuguese shorter, no loss); 49:11 −3/+3 (the Latin order *mecum est* kept at the end); 49:21 +4/+3 (*iniquamente* and *semelhante a ti* are the words; *como tu* would save three syllables but lose símilis's word, which 48:13 keeps as *semelhante*); 49:23 +5 (the supplied *está*; the verbless option is 2 syllables shorter).

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context). 30 readings; unknown: manifestamente, holocaustos, plenitude, Imola, narras, iniquamente, arrebate. One taken: 49:8 porém heard as a reproach. manifestamente replaced (with the stylist). holocausto, plenitude, arrebatar are glossary words already recorded as unknown to earlier readers; Imola and iniquamente noted in their decisions. 49:4 separar heard as set apart — the D42 cost; julgar remains the option. 49:5 aliança heard as ring as well as covenant, and firmam heard as sealed — as meant.
